contributions.detail: delta 1,150.00, FULLY EXPLAINED BY THE FORM ITSELF. This filer's Schedule A prints three summary lines: 'Total Above $50  $4,525.00', 'Total Below $50  $1,150.00', and 'TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED  $5,675.00'. The 24 itemized rows sum to 4,525.00, matching the 'Total Above $50' line EXACTLY; the remaining 1,150.00 is the filer's aggregate of sub-$50 contributions, which is not itemized anywhere on the form and therefore has no donor rows to transcribe. Nothing is missing from the transcription - the itemized side is complete and the delta is a real, printed, unitemizable aggregate.

itemized.notes: NOT the pre-printed county form: this filer typed her own LANDSCAPE Schedule A and Schedule B (headed 'Pg. 3 of 4' / 'Pg. 4 of 4', Turner, 6/20/2006), which poppler renders horizontally with no rotation needed. SCHEDULE A CARRIES AN UNITEMIZED AGGREGATE LINE ('Total Below $50  $1,150.00') beside the itemized total - see the recon detail; that 1,150.00 is a printed field of the form, not a set of rows I failed to read, and it is deliberately NOT emitted as a row because it names no donor. SCHEDULE B USES NON-STANDARD COLUMN HEADS - Date / Description / Amount / Notes - so 'Description' was mapped to vendor_raw and 'Notes' to purpose; the field-shift screen was run and every one of the 11 rows has all four cells populated in that mapping. One Schedule B row names no payee at all ('Check Fee'), kept verbatim. ADDRESS BLOCK: the four ORGANISATIONAL donors (Local 222, Salt Lake County Democratic Party x2, WVC Mortgage, Wasatch Pacific) print a full address and their printed city abbreviation ('SLC', 'WVC') plus state are recorded; every INDIVIDUAL donor's address cells are empty, and faint ghost characters survive beneath two of those rows, which indicates the block was whited out rather than never filled - those rows are treated as redacted. No street address or PO box is written anywhere in this record. Typos are retained verbatim from the form ('Salt Lake Couny Dems', 'Reimbursment', 'evenlopes', 'Remitance', 'Dayzz').
